### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 222755ebbf20c564b85d3da9e04f1bd9ebcbf280`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **151** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 222755ebbf20c564b85d3da9e04f1bd9ebcbf280` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7927ddd575937a2b86ca405317f07762e455960f` — the merge of head `6ba5f8cc3ea2ea0cb52f8a5c328e043f241380bd` into base `222755ebbf20c564b85d3da9e04f1bd9ebcbf280`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7927ddd575937a2b86ca405317f07762e455960f && git checkout 7927ddd575937a2b86ca405317f07762e455960f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 222755ebbf20c564b85d3da9e04f1bd9ebcbf280 6ba5f8cc3ea2ea0cb52f8a5c328e043f241380bd && git checkout -B drift-repro 222755ebbf20c564b85d3da9e04f1bd9ebcbf280 && git merge --no-ff 6ba5f8cc3ea2ea0cb52f8a5c328e043f241380bd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 222755ebbf20c564b85d3da9e04f1bd9ebcbf280
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 222755ebbf20c564b85d3da9e04f1bd9ebcbf280` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6ba5f8cc3ea2ea0cb52f8a5c328e043f241380bd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts, packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts, packages/rest/src/error-response.ts (read, unchanged), packages/types/src/response-envelope.ts (read, unchanged), packages/client/src/index.ts, .changeset/26314-record-anchored-approval-lock-read.md, content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/record-lock-read.integration.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-approvals-record-lock-route.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-record-lock-read.dogfood.test.ts. The remainder of the diff (packages/client/src/client.test.ts, packages/rest/src/execctx-consumer-census.test.ts) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

Base: merge-base with origin/main is `1a298dda8d9a36e0c594a1f219277110fc939f43`; six commits on the head, two of them merges of main. Inputs read: card #26314 body and all three comments (6427176260 triage, 6427951121 claim, 6429820983 os-dev-report), rulings 6422939157 and 6419712936 on #25934 and 5299823744 on #8652, PR #26361 body, file list and net diff, and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. `IApprovalService` gains one OPTIONAL member, `getRecordLock?(object, recordId, context)`, answering a promise of `{ locked: boolean }` or `null`. Widening only: every existing implementation, and the spec's own `minimalService` test literal (approval-service.test.ts:228), still satisfies the interface. No exported schema or type is added. The spec's generated surfaces (api-surface/contracts.json, api-surface-signatures.json) list export names, not interface members, so no artifact regeneration is owed; `Spec property liveness` and the lint gates are green. RIGHT.

2. Claim "read AS THE CALLER (object read, then row-level access)": `ApprovalService.getRecordLock` (approval-service.ts:8673) calls `this.engine.find(objectName, { where: { id }, fields: ['id'], limit: 1, context })`, byte-for-byte the anchor read of `addRecordReaderVisibleIds` (:8392), the #8652 precedent. The caller's context is the one the door resolved; no `SYSTEM_CTX` on this path. RIGHT.

3. Claim "unreadable equals missing, no path tells them apart": three outcomes exist and every one is id-independent in the order it is reached. (a) Object read refused: the engine throws before any id-dependent step; the door relays it through `handleRouteError` at the refusal's own status, the same status for an existing or a missing id. (b) Object read allowed but the row is filtered by RLS, or does not exist: one and the same `find` returns `[]`, `getRecordLock` answers `null`, and the door writes one `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` whose message names the object only (`No such 'object' record`), never the id. (c) Row visible: `200 { success: true, data: { locked } }`. The pending-request lookup runs only after (c), so neither its result nor its timing is observable for an unreadable record, and the lock judgement never consults the caller. The integration test pins (a) and (b) at the service (unreadable `_b` equals `MISSING`; outsider gets `PERMISSION_DENIED 403` for both ids), the route test pins one 404 body with the id absent, and the dogfood run pins (b) and (c) through the real `SecurityPlugin` on `private` objects, status and body equal for the stranger's unreadable id and a non-existent id. RIGHT. Coverage note, not a defect: arm (a) is exercised end to end only with a stand-in middleware (integration) and a mocked rejection (route test); with the real `SecurityPlugin` the dogfood stranger holds object read narrowed to own rows, so the real plugin's denial shape at the door is judged by reading `resolveErrorResponse` (status carried through), not by a test. The property holds structurally because the throw precedes every id-dependent step.

4. Claim "one lock judgement shared with the beforeUpdate hook and lock_record": `nodeConfigLocksRecord` (lifecycle-hooks.ts:403) is the only executable spelling of `lockRecord !== false` in the plugin's non-test sources (a git grep at the head finds the rule's text otherwise only in two comments and the function's own doc block). Its three callers are the hook (:592), the request row mirror `rowFromRequest` (approval-service.ts:1290) and the read (`recordHeldByLockingApproval`, :439). RIGHT.

5. Claim "shares the hook's lookup": `recordHeldByLockingApproval` calls `pendingRequestsForRecords(engine, object, [id])`, which for one id delegates to `pendingRequestFor` (limit 1, `SYSTEM_CTX`); the hook's by-id path is `gatingRequests` → `asIdList(ctx.input.id)` → the same `pendingRequestsForRecords`. The bookkeeping-object exemption is one function, `isApprovalBookkeepingObject`, used by both. The read deliberately omits the hook's two WRITE-scoped exemptions (the opening run's own writes, mirror-only writes); those are properties of a writer and a payload, not of the record, and the doc block says so. RIGHT.

6. Import direction: approval-service.ts now imports from lifecycle-hooks.js; lifecycle-hooks.ts imports nothing from approval-service.ts (its local imports are `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/spec/data`, `./payload-redaction.js`). No cycle. RIGHT.

7. Public REST surface: `GET /api/v1/approvals/records/:object/:recordId/lock`, ledgered as `sdk` with client `approvals.getRecordLock`, registered under the same `dataPath` and `isScoped` convention as the sibling approval routes. The door serves `{ locked: lock.locked === true }` and drops any extra key an implementation hands back. Closed query set is `APPROVAL_RECORD_LOCK_PARAMS = []`, refused via `refuseUnknownQueryParams` with the located 400 before the service is asked. RIGHT.

8. Claim "501 on absence": `if (!svc || typeof svc.getRecordLock !== 'function') return respond501(res)`, the family's existing helper. Note only: the 501 body is the family's flat `{ code, message }` dialect while the 404 and 400 are the nested envelope; that is the pre-existing shape of every approval route's 501, not something this diff introduces. RIGHT.

9. Client: `client.approvals.getRecordLock(object, recordId)` encodes both path segments and unwraps the envelope; pinned by client.test.ts. Docs paragraph in approvals.mdx states the same contract as the door (404 for unreadable equals missing, 501 on absence, `locked` only). RIGHT.

10. The route's `resolveExecCtx` site is bare and guarded by `enforceAuth` on the next line, so the execctx census moves 61 → 62 sites, 45 → 46 bare, 144 → 145 mentions. RIGHT by construction; the census test is in the CI test run.

11. Disclosure posture against the rulings: `{ locked }` only; no request id, node, participants or `pending`; `listRequests` and `getRequest` for the non-participant still answer `[]` and `null` (integration test), the request list through the door still answers `[]` for the editor (dogfood). #8652 ruling 5299823744 is untouched; #25934 ruling A parameters (a) carrier, (b) disclosure to every reader as the caller, (c) payload are each met. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/26314-record-anchored-approval-lock-read.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/client`, the four packages the diff moves. Both declaration lines are present and identical on the PR body and the changeset body: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The kind is `none` (a service contract member, a route and a client method; nothing an author writes in metadata changes), and by the level rule `none` takes `patch`. The widening arm is right: an optional member added, a route added, a method added; nothing removed, renamed, refused or tightened, so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

Clause-②: yes (widening), matched.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags from the PR body (Deviations, Acceptance notes) and the os-dev-report 6429820983 (`deviations`, `out_of_scope_findings`; `open_questions` is empty):

- Deviation 1, route, ledger row and client method live in packages/rest and packages/client, not plugin-approvals: ANSWERED. `approvals-routes.ts` and `rest-route-ledger.ts` are where every approval route and ledger row lives; the claim comment itself names the ledger and `IApprovalService`, and the seat agreed the `sdk` row before the change. The right files were touched.
- Deviation 2, skill teaching deferred because `skills/**` is Tier H: ESCALATED to the seat. Triage 6427176260 requires the PR or "a follow-up card it names" to teach the new route with an eval prompt. The report carries a proposed card title and dedupe words but no filed card number, so nothing is named yet. The seat files that card (skills/objectstack-automation: the lock read plus one eval prompt) so the deferral has a number, before or at landing. Not a defect of this diff.
- Acceptance note 1, `pendingRequestFor` reads with `limit: 1`: ANSWERED. The read and the hook share that lookup (①.5), so they cannot disagree; and the service refuses a second pending request on one record (`DUPLICATE_REQUEST`, approval-service.ts:3602 and :5451), so the "two pending requests on one record" case is refused upstream of both. No card owed.
- Acceptance note 2, overlap with open #26337 on approval-service.ts and approvals.mdx: ANSWERED. Different regions; the single-writer-path check is green on this head; whichever lands second merges main.
- PR body "Spec change: needs the spec seat's sign-off" (also triage's lane note and the claim's "the seat obtains the spec seat's sign-off before landing"): this record is the contract-tier review of the spec hunk on its merits (①.1 to ①.3) and finds it sound; the lane sign-off itself is the seat's process obligation and stays ESCALATED to the seat as outstanding until it is recorded.
- Dogfood does not run on PR CI; the new dogfood file and the two ablations were run by the dev locally under the verify lock. Noted; this review ran nothing locally.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-10-26T23:37:50Z: 46 runs, 27 success, 7 skipped (opt-in and matrix placeholders), 0 failure, 12 in progress (Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check UI, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check workspace). Green at that time includes Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, every Lint job, the claim and single-writer-path checks, Type Check source gates and debt ledger. The landing rule still requires every check green; this verdict is on the diff and the contract, with those twelve conclusions recorded as not yet read.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-rzpauf`
Reviewed-by: `session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`

**VERDICT: PASS**

1. **Shape:** a draft against `main`. The body carries `Fixes #26314`, and `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial, identical to the changeset `.changeset/26314-record-anchored-approval-lock-read.md` (`patch` on spec, plugin-approvals, rest and client, the four packages the diff publishes from). `check-governed-merges --pr 26361`: NOT governed (0 of 13 paths), 907 changed lines.
2. **Contract review:** the diff touches `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts`, so the at-tier review was owed (schema face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`). Its record is comment `6429948897` on this PR, on head `6ba5f8cc3e`: **PASS**. Under pm-dispatch `cross-repo-coordination.md` (a spec surface found inside a dispatched card stays on the card and is reviewed at tier), that record is the spec half's review; the order's separate spec-seat sign-off is withdrawn by the seat that wrote it.
3. **Rulings checked against the diff (the seat's own reading of the non-spec remainder):**
   - **Disclosure as the caller:** `ApprovalService.getRecordLock` reads the record with `engine.find` under the caller's context (`fields: ['id']`, `limit: 1`). Empty answers `null`; the route turns every `null` into one `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` body that names neither the id nor the cause. A caller with no read on the object is refused before any id-dependent step, the same for every id.
   - **Payload:** the route sends `{ locked: lock.locked === true }` and nothing else; the rest test pins that extra keys from a service are dropped.
   - **One lock judgement:** `nodeConfigLocksRecord` in `lifecycle-hooks.ts` is the only spelling of `lockRecord !== false`. The `beforeUpdate` hook, the `lock_record` mirror in `rowFromRequest` and the new read all call it, and the read shares the hook's pending-request lookup.
   - **#8652 untouched:** request content stays behind `approvalsVisibleToReaders`; the dogfood case asserts the non-participant still lists `[]`.
   - **Route rules:** the closed query-parameter set is empty and refused with the located `400`; a service without the member answers `501`; the ledger row ships as `sdk` with `approvals.getRecordLock`.
   - **Tests and ablations:** the card's four cases run through the REST door on a real boot (dogfood, run locally under the verify lock since dogfood does not run on PR CI). Ablating the lock judgement reds `:217`, and ablating the as-caller read reds `:209`, each confirmed in `dist` by the ablation preflight.
4. **Gates:** at this stamp the head's 48 check-runs read 41 success and 7 skipped (path-filtered UI, dogfood matrix placeholders and opt-in harnesses), with none failing or in progress; `Test Core` 1–8, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green; mergeable, clean. Locally the dev reports all 114 derived gate commands exit 0, reconciled with `--ran` (0 not measured), and the new dogfood file 1 of 1 passing.
5. **Accepted deviations:**
   - The route, ledger row and client method live in `packages/rest` and `packages/client`, outside the claim's plugin-approvals surface. The seat agreed this before the change so the ledger row ships as `sdk`, not as a gap.
   - Skill teaching is not in this PR, because `skills/**` is governed and would put the whole PR behind maintainer approval. The order allowed a named follow-up card; it is filed as #26362 (`domain:skills`, blocked by this PR).
6. **Out of scope:** #26362 above. The `limit: 1` note in the body is answered by the contract review: the service refuses a second pending request on one record (`DUPLICATE_REQUEST`). #26337 overlaps `approval-service.ts` and `approvals.mdx` in other regions; whichever lands second merges `main`.
